summary: A six-line hotfix disabled the statement timeout on orders reads instead of raising it, so slow queries ran until the 30s gateway timeout and 11% of order reads returned 504. Vigil ranked the hotfix above an 800-line refactor that landed in the same window.

timeline.event: Hotfix f6a7b8c9d0 deployed: statement_timeout set to '0' on the orders read session.
OrderQueryTimeouts alert fired for orders (11% of reads timing out at 30s).
Vigil brief posted: culprit f6a7b8c9d0 at 0.87 confidence; the 800-line repository refactor ranked second at 0.09.
Incident marked resolved after the hotfix was reverted and long-running queries were cancelled.

root_cause: Retries during a backlog drain were tripping the 5s statement timeout. The hotfix removed the cancellation entirely with SET statement_timeout = '0' rather than raising it, so slow reads held their connections until the gateway timed out at 30s.
contributing_factors: The hotfix shipped outside the normal review path because it was labelled urgent.
The underlying retry storm was never addressed, only its symptom.
impact: 11% of order reads returned 504 for the duration, against a 450 requests/minute orders baseline; customers could not load order history.
resolution: Reverted f6a7b8c9d0 to restore the 5s timeout and cancelled the queries still running past 30s.
went_well: Message signals and diff size worked as intended: a six-line hotfix outranked an 800-line refactor that shipped in the same window.
The revert was clean because the hotfix touched one file.
went_poorly: 'Urgent' bypassed review for a change to a global safety limit.
Disabling a timeout was available as a one-line change with no guardrail.

action_items.description: Fix the retry path that was tripping the 5s timeout during backlog drains.
Reject statement_timeout values of 0 in code review with a lint rule.
Require a second reviewer for hotfixes that touch database session setup.
